summary: Great Mills 120-ft steel lookout, built 1933; by 2006 the property went to St. Mary's County and the tower was moved to the Lathrop E. Smith center in Montgomery County.

facts.design: 120-ft galvanized steel lookout tower, steel throughout (Midland Journal and Evening Star, 1933, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
facts.status_note: The original Great Mills hilltop is listed as gone; the tower structure was reassembled at the Lathrop E. Smith Environmental Education Center, Montgomery County. DNR gives no date for the move.

access.note: The tower now stands at a Montgomery County Public Schools outdoor education site; the sources read describe school programs, not public visits.

events.note: Erected in summer 1933 as a 120-ft galvanized steel lookout (Midland Journal, Nov 10, 1933); the Evening Star of Nov 18, 1933 reported it had just been completed as the tallest fire tower west of Chesapeake Bay in Maryland
DNR had transferred ownership of the entire property to St. Mary's County by 2006
Structure removed and reassembled for new duties at the Lathrop E. Smith Environmental Education Center, Montgomery County; DNR gives no date

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA lists the original site as gone and the Lathrop tower as standing with its cab missing; DNR says the structure was removed and reassembled there. The sources agree once the cab note is read.

Wildfire History says Maryland towers were 80 to 100 feet tall; the later DNR draft report says state forestry towers typically ranged from 50 to 120 feet. The story gives both and does not call this tower unique.

notes_for_editor: Covers the original Great Mills hilltop. The destination tower (us-md-great-mills-at-lathrop-e-smith-env-ed-center) already has its own story from 2026-10-09; this one does not repeat it at length. No staffing or fire sources were found for Great Mills, so none are written. The 1933 build facts rest on newspaper text quoted by the Forest Lookouts page, not on scans. The DNR draft gives no date for the move.
